ru: На спекта́кле мы бу́дем хохота́ть до слёз.
note: Compound future correctly rendered as 'will be laughing'; 'until we cry' is the natural English for до слёз.

ru: Я хохота́ла бы над ка́ждой шу́ткой.
note: Imperfective бы + past with no protasis reads as a habitual present counterfactual, so plain 'would laugh' is right.

en: I laugh loudly at his jokes.
note: 'Guffaw' is not the headword gloss the tap-hint shows and every sibling sentence uses 'laugh loudly'.
Same words reordered to the commoner English adverb position, so the word-bank tiles still assemble it.

ru: С понеде́льника я бу́ду целова́ть тебя́ ка́ждое у́тро.
note: Imperfective compound future correctly kept as 'will be kissing'.

en: Mum kisses the child before bed.
note: 'Before sleep' is translationese; 'before bed' is what an English speaker writes for перед сном.

Frame collision only: the imperfective habitual 'would kiss' is the correct reading here, and 'her hands' vs the perfective's 'you goodbye' still cues the drill; the perfective partner is the side to fix.

ru: Будь инструме́нты, я чини́л бы кран сам.
note: Present counterfactual with an imperfective, so plain 'would mend' is right; the added 'I' is required by the English conditional.

ru: Все выходны́е мы бу́дем чини́ть ста́рый велосипе́д.
en: All weekend we will be mending the old bicycle.
note: 'Will spend the whole weekend mending' invents a verb the Russian never uses; the compound future бу́дем чини́ть is simply 'will be mending'.

ru: Будь у меня́ вре́мя, я чита́ла бы бо́льше.
note: Frame collision only: the imperfective present counterfactual 'would read more' is correct, and the perfective partner ('in one night') is the side that should read 'would have read'.
Relative clause is the only way English renders the present active participle.
English imperative cannot mark aspect, but 'every day' carries the habitual cue that distinguishes it from the perfective partner.
Frame match is harmless: an infinitive after 'like' can only be imperfective in Russian.

en: Yesterday we were reading an interesting story.
note: Bare 'read' is aspect-neutral and collides with прочитать's 'I read this book in a week'; the progressive commits to the imperfective activity reading.

ru: За́втра ве́чером я бу́ду чита́ть кни́гу.
note: Compound future correctly rendered 'will be reading'.
Imperative frame match is unavoidable in English; subject and object differ from the perfective partner, so the cue survives.

ru: Я чу́вствовал бы себя́ споко́йнее до́ма.
note: Imperfective present counterfactual state, so 'would feel' is right; the perfective partner ('joy at that moment') is the side that should read 'would have felt'.
'He feels tiredness' is not English; the adjective is the only natural rendering.

ru: По́сле о́тдыха ты бу́дешь чу́вствовать себя́ лу́чше.
note: 'You will be feeling better' is idiomatic English here, so the compound future keeps its progressive.

ru: По го́рной тропе́ мы бу́дем шага́ть друг за дру́гом.
en: Along the mountain trail we will be striding one after another.
note: Flattens the compound future to 'will walk' and swaps the headword sense ('stride') for 'walk single file'; the literal rendering is still natural English.

ru: Будь доро́га ро́вной, я шага́л бы быстре́е.

note: 'March' is the established English for soldiers шагают; forcing 'stride' would read worse.

ru: Я шага́ю по тропи́нке в лесу́.

note: 'Don't stir' would mean stirring a liquid; 'Don't move' is the natural imperative for шевелиться.

ru: Я не шевели́лась бы во вре́мя съёмки.
en: I would not stir during the photo shoot.
note: 'During the photo' is not English; съёмка is the shoot/session, not the resulting picture.
ве́тер takes the second locative after на — «на ветру́»; «на ве́тре» is not what a native speaker says (the English needs no change).

ru: На ве́тре ли́стья бу́дут ти́хо шевели́ться.
ru_new: На ветру́ ли́стья бу́дут ти́хо шевели́ться.
note: Same second-locative problem: «на ветру́», not «на ве́тре»; the English 'will be stirring' is already correct for the compound future.

en: The children were whispering something in his ear.
note: Simple 'whispered' collides with both прошептать sentences; the progressive commits to the imperfective and keeps the possessive English cannot omit.
'His' is added, but English requires a possessor with 'in the ear'; the Russian на у́хо leaves it implicit.

ru: Е́сли бы уме́л, я шил бы сам.
note: The added 'it' is forced by English — 'I would sew myself' would mean stitching one's own body.
Imperfective habitual correctly rendered 'used to sew'.

ru: Она́ бу́дет шить костю́м всю неде́лю.
en: She will be sewing the suit all week.
note: костю́м is glossed 'suit' corpus-wide, which the tap-hint shows; 'costume' is a narrower guess the sentence does not support.

ru: Всю ночь мо́ре бу́дет шуме́ть за окно́м.
note: Compound future correctly rendered 'will be making noise'.

en: The sea was making noise all night.
note: 'Roaring' is not the headword sense the tap-hint shows, and the parallel future sentence already uses 'making noise'.

ru: Я не шуме́л бы так по́здно.
Я не шути́ла бы над э́той те́мой.
За́втра на вечери́нке мы бу́дем шути́ть.
note: Compound future correctly rendered 'will be joking'.

ru: За́втра я щёлкну па́льцами, и начнётся му́зыка.
note: 'Click one's fingers' is the standard British collocation and matches the headword gloss.

ru: Будь темно́, я щёлкнула бы вы́ключателем.
note: Protasis is present ('if it were dark'), so the perfective stays 'would click' — a single event, not 'would have clicked'.
'Snap my fingers' is the idiomatic English for щёлкнуть па́льцами.

ru: Он яви́лся на собра́ние без опозда́ния.
en: He turned up to the meeting without being late.
note: 'Without delay' means immediately; без опозда́ния (опозда́ние = lateness) says he was not late.

ru: Я явлю́сь за́втра к девяти́ часа́м.
en_alt: Tomorrow I will appear by nine o'clock.
note: Same words in the Russian's own order, so the word-bank tiles assemble it.

ru: Зна́я о встре́че, я яви́лся бы ра́ньше.
en: I would have appeared earlier if I had known about the meeting.
note: Perfective бы + past over an already-past meeting is a past counterfactual regret, not the present 'if I knew' the English states.

ru: Без него́ прое́кт не явля́лся бы по́лным.
Ско́ро он бу́дет явля́ться дире́ктором фи́рмы.
en: Soon he will be the director of the firm.
note: фи́рма is glossed 'firm' and the parallel present-tense sentence says 'firm'; no progressive is possible here since 'will be being' is not English.
